literal: Industriousness called excellence-in rests-indeed beneficence called greatness.
translation: The noble pride of being a benefactor rests entirely on the excellent quality of industriousness.
modern: பிறருக்கு உதவி செய்யும் வேளாண்மை என்னும் பெருமிதம், ஒருவருடைய விடாமுயற்சி என்னும் உயர்ந்த பண்பின் மேலேயே நிலைபெற்றுள்ளது.
explanation: This couplet connects the capacity to help others with the habit of hard work. The word 'vēḷāṇmai' refers to beneficence or philanthropy, while 'tāḷāṇmai' means relentless effort or industriousness. The poet explains that the noble pride ('cerukku') of being a benefactor rests entirely on the excellent foundation of personal effort. Without working hard to gather resources, one cannot experience the greatness of giving to those in need. Here, 'cerukku', which often means arrogance, is used positively to denote the dignified joy of helping others.
